The Evidence Packet: the location records relied on above, and how they were compared.

paragraphs.text: I am Lin Quintaro, the defendant in this action. I reside at 104 HILLSIDE AVENUE, Queens, NY 11697. I make this affidavit in support of my application to vacate the default judgment entered against me.

An affidavit of service has been filed in this action. It states that service was made upon me by M. Grisholm on September 9, 2025 at 4:30 PM, at 104 HILLSIDE AVENUE, Queens, NY 11697, by affixing to the door, and mailing, under CPLR 308(4). A copy is annexed as Exhibit A.
I was not served with the summons and complaint in this action. No papers were delivered to me on September 9, 2025, and I did not learn of this action until long after that date.
104 HILLSIDE AVENUE, Queens, NY 11697, the address at which service is claimed, was not my dwelling place, my usual place of abode or my place of business on that date.
I keep a location history. The records I rely on below are recorded stays in one place. They are annexed as part of Exhibit B, in full for the hours around the time sworn to.

My location history records me in one place from 2:00 PM to 10:00 PM on September 9, 2025, which includes 4:30 PM, the time of the service sworn to. That place is 12.8 km from 104 HILLSIDE AVENUE, Queens, NY 11697.
The delivery and the mailing must be within 20 days of each other. The affidavit of service shows 34 days between them.

Papers may be affixed to a door and mailed only where the defendant cannot be served in person, or by delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion, with due diligence. The affidavit of service records 2 earlier attempts, on 2 days. I respectfully ask the court to consider whether that satisfies due diligence.

The comparison of my location records with the affidavit of service, the distances and times relied on above, and the method by which they were calculated, are set out in the Evidence Packet annexed as Exhibit B.
On these facts the court did not acquire personal jurisdiction over me, and the judgment entered against me should be vacated under CPLR 5015(a)(4).

In the alternative, I was served, if at all, by affixing to the door, and mailing, under CPLR 308(4), and not by personal delivery. I did not personally receive notice of this action in time to defend it. I have a meritorious defence to this action: I never opened an account with this company. I therefore ask the court to allow me to defend under CPLR 317.
That application is made within the time allowed, which runs to March 14, 2027.
Because the facts of service are disputed, I respectfully request a traverse hearing at which the process server may be examined.
I respectfully request that enforcement of the judgment, including any restraint on my bank account or wages, be stayed while this application is decided.

A process server licensed in New York City must carry a device that electronically records the location, date and time of every service and every attempt. I respectfully request that the plaintiff be directed to produce that record for the service and attempts described in the affidavit of service.

deadlines.note: If you were served in any way other than in person, and you did not personally get notice in time to defend the case, you may be able to ask the court to reopen it within one year of learning about the judgment, and no more than five years after it was entered. You also have to show you have a defence worth hearing. For you that is one year after you found out, which is March 14, 2027 and five years after the judgment was entered, which is August 1, 2030. The earlier of the two is the one that matters. A judgment can be reopened when the court did not have jurisdiction, which includes service that was not done properly. There is no stated one-year limit for that ground, but act promptly.

findings.detail: Your location history has you in one place from 2:00 PM to 10:00 PM on September 9, 2025, and that place is 12.8 km from the address on the affidavit. The service claimed at 4:30 PM on September 9, 2025 falls inside that stay.
findings.title: Your phone was somewhere else at that time

findings.detail: The delivery and the mailing have to be within 20 days of each other. This affidavit shows 34 days between them.
findings.legal_ref: CPLR 308(4) — affixing to the door, and mailing
findings.title: The mailing is 34 days from the delivery

findings.detail: Papers may only be taped to a door and mailed when the server could not serve you in person or leave them with someone at your address, after trying with due diligence. Courts commonly expect three attempts, on at least two different days, at different times of day. Here, the affidavit shows 2 attempts and all of them fall on a weekday between 9 AM and 5 PM. This is worth asking a lawyer or the Court Help Center about.

packet.fixes_note: All 98 location records used in this check are listed. They are the records close in time to the sworn moments above; the rest of your location history was never sent off the device it was read on.
packet.intro: This packet compares the affidavit of service filed against Lin Quintaro, index number CV-055084-25/QU, with the location records you supplied. It sets out what the affidavit claims, what your records show, and where the two cannot both be true. It draws no conclusion about what happened, and it is not a finding of fact.

verdict.claimed: The affidavit swears that you were served at 4:30 PM on September 9, 2025 at 104 HILLSIDE AVENUE, Queens, NY 11697, by affixing to the door, and mailing, under CPLR 308(4).
verdict.headline: Your location data conflicts with the affidavit.
verdict.label: Conflicts
verdict.line: Your nearest location record is 12.8 km from that address.
verdict.meaning: Your own records put you away from the address on the affidavit at the time the server swore to, by more than the margins set out under “How this was worked out”.
